**Q3 2026 revenue:** Equinix had not yet reported Q3 as of October 17, 2026; it scheduled its earnings call for October 28, so the relevant company figure is its Q3 revenue guide of **$2.525–$2.575 billion** (midpoint **$2.550 billion**), representing **9–11% year-over-year reported growth** and **10–12% normalized/constant-currency growth**. [[1, 2]] 
The available analyst consensus was **$2.618 billion**, about **$43 million (1.7%) above** the high end of management’s range and **2.7% above** its midpoint, implying the principal near-term revenue-execution risk was expectations above formal guidance. [[3, 2]]

**Why AI demand appears material:** In Q2, Equinix said AI infrastructure demand was accelerating and that the vast majority of its largest deals were AI-workload driven; management characterized the demand as spanning private AI stacks, sovereign deployments, batch training/inference, and latency-sensitive inference. [[4]] 
This is not solely a hyperscaler-compute story: Equinix’s differentiated proposition is neutral, connected infrastructure, and the company stated that eight of the top 10 AI model providers and eight of the top 10 neoclouds use its platform for key networking workloads. [[4]]

[[5]] 
That leasing was financially consequential: Q2 revenue was **$2.625 billion**, up **16% year over year**, and management explicitly attributed part of that growth to one-time xScale fees; the Hampton xScale transaction alone contributed about **$120 million** of non-recurring fees. [[2, 6]] 
Accordingly, xScale validates substantial AI/hyperscale demand and supports future capacity utilization, but investors should distinguish recurring underlying demand from the timing volatility created by non-recurring leasing fees. [[2, 6]]

**Interconnection is the stronger recurring-demand indicator:** Equinix delivered **$424 million of annualized gross bookings**, up **23% year over year**, and added a record **9,700 net interconnections** in Q2. [[2]]

events.content:
**Equinix — Recent Revenue and AI‑Driven Leasing Demand (Q2 2026 / Q3 2026 guide)**  

| Metric | Period | Figure | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Revenue guide (Q3 2026)** | Q3 2026 (guidance) | $2.525–$2.575 B (midpoint $2.550 B); 9–11% YoY reported growth | S1.1 |
| **Q2 2026 actual revenue** | Q2 2026 | $2.625 B; +16% YoY (includes ~$120 M non‑recurring xScale fees from the Hampton transaction) | S1.2, S1.6 |
| **xScale leasing (Q2 2026)** | Q2 2026 | 134 MW signed across the Americas; xScale portfolio total 604 MW leased; ~2,000 MW when fully built out; >$23 B total investment | S1.5, S1.6 |
| **Annualized gross bookings** | Q2 2026 | $424 M; +23% YoY | S1.1, S1.2 |
| **Net interconnections** | Q2 2026 | Record 9,700 added; +11% YoY MRR growth (reported & constant‑currency) | S1.1, S1.2 |
| **AI‑provider concentration** | Q2 2026 | Eight of the top 10 AI model providers and eight of the top 10 neoclouds use Equinix for key networking workloads | S1.4 |

**Key take‑aways**

- Equinix’s Q3 2026 revenue guide points to continued double‑digit growth, driven by underlying MRR expansion (≈11% constant‑currency).  
- AI demand is a material factor: the company notes that the majority of its largest deals are AI‑workload driven, and the top AI model/neocloud providers rely on its platform for networking.  
- xScale leasing is the clearest quantitative signal of AI/hyperscale demand: 134 MW signed in Q2 2026 adds to a 604 MW leased portfolio, with ~$23 B of capital invested. The Hampton transaction alone contributed ~$120 M in non‑recurring fees to Q2 revenue.  
- Recurring interconnection demand is also strong: $424 M annualized gross bookings and a record 9,700 net interconnections in Q2, with 11% YoY MRR growth, indicating that AI is also fueling connectivity needs beyond raw compute leases.  

All figures are sourced from Equinix’s Q2 2026 earnings release, guidance slides, and the Q2 2026 earnings call transcript.

tool_arguments.query: Equinix dividend per share and REIT payout policy FY 2025 Q2

events.content: Equinix dividend per share and REIT payout policy FY 2025 Q2

**FY2025 Q2 dividend per share:** Equinix paid a quarterly common-stock cash dividend of **$4.69 per share**, paid on **June 18, 2025** to shareholders of record on **May 21, 2025**. [[1]]

**REIT payout policy:** In its Q2 2025 Form 10-Q, Equinix stated that it expected its **2025 quarterly and other applicable distributions to equal or exceed REIT taxable income recognized in 2025**. [[2]] Equinix elected REIT tax status beginning in 2015; dividends paid are generally deductible against taxable income of the REIT and qualified REIT subsidiaries, while taxable REIT subsidiaries remain subject to corporate income tax. [[1]] 

Thus, the relevant policy is not a fixed percentage of GAAP earnings or AFFO; it is to distribute at least its REIT taxable income—consistent with maintaining REIT qualification—with the company indicating an intention to distribute the entire taxable income generated by its REIT and qualified REIT subsidiaries for 2025. [[1]]

Related coverage:
**Equinix (EQIX) dividend:** the current quarterly common-stock dividend is **$5.16 per share**, a 10% increase, payable March 18, 2026 to shareholders of record February 25, 2026. [[1]] 
Annualizing that rate implies **$20.64 per share**, subject to future board declarations. [[1]] 

For comparison, Equinix distributed **$4.69 per share per quarter**, or **$18.76 annualized**, during 2025. [[2]]

**REIT payout:** a REIT must distribute at least **90% of REIT taxable income**—calculated before the dividends-paid deduction and excluding net capital gains—to preserve REIT qualification; this is a tax-income test, not an AFFO payout-ratio target. [[3]] [[4]] 

Using Equinix’s 2026 guidance, expected cash dividends of approximately **$2.036 billion** represent about **48.0%–49.0% of guided AFFO** of $4.158–$4.238 billion; on a per-share basis, the $20.64 annualized dividend is about **48.3%–49.2%** of guided diluted AFFO per share of $41.93–$42.74. [[5]] 

Thus, Equinix’s cash dividend is roughly a **48%–49% AFFO payout**, while its legally required REIT distribution percentage is measured against taxable income and is at least 90%. [[5]] [[3]]

events.content:
**Equinix — Dividend & REIT Payout Policy (FY 2025 – 2026)**  

| Metric | Period | Figure | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Quarterly common‑stock dividend** | Q2 2025 | $4.69 per share (paid June 18 2025) | S8.1 |
| **Quarterly common‑stock dividend** | Q1 2026 (most recent increase) | $5.16 per share (10% increase from Q2 2025; payable March 18 2026) | S8.3 |
| **Annualized dividend rate** | 2026 | $20.64 per share (based on $5.16 × 4) | S8.1, S8.3 |
| **2025 annualized dividend** | 2025 | $18.76 per share (based on $4.69 × 4) | S8.2 |
| **Expected 2026 cash dividend outlay** | FY 2026 guidance | ~$2.036 B total cash dividends | S8.5 |
| **Guided AFFO (FY 2026)** | FY 2026 | $4.158–$4.238 B | S8.5 |
| **Cash‑dividend payout vs. AFFO** | FY 2026 | 48.0%–49.0% of guided AFFO (≈$2.036 B ÷ $4.158–4.238 B) | S8.5 |
| **Per‑share AFFO payout** | FY 2026 | $20.64 ÷ $41.93–$42.74 = 48.3%–49.2% of guided diluted AFFO per share | S8.5 |
| **REIT qualification requirement** | Ongoing | Must distribute ≥ 90% of REIT taxable income (calculated before the dividends‑paid deduction, excluding net capital gains) | S8.2, S8.4 |
| **Equinix’s stated distribution intention** | 2025 | Expected 2025 quarterly and other applicable distributions to equal or exceed 2025 REIT taxable income | S8.2 |

**Key take‑aways**

- Equinix has increased its quarterly dividend for 11 consecutive years since its REIT conversion, raising it from $4.69 (Q2 2025) to $5.16 (Q1 2026), a 10% step‑up.  
- The company’s **cash dividend is roughly 48%–49% of guided AFFO**, a level that comfortably exceeds the **minimum 90% of REIT taxable income** required for REIT qualification.  
- The REIT payout policy is **not a fixed AFFO ratio** but a **tax‑income test**: Equinix targets distributions that equal or exceed its REIT taxable income each year, thereby maintaining its REIT status.  
- For 2026, the projected $2.036 B in cash dividends represents about **48%–49%** of the $4.158–4.238 B guided AFFO, and about **48.3%–49.2%** on a per‑share basis.

function.arguments: {"query":"Equinix dividend per share and REIT payout policy FY 2025 Q2"}

private_messages.content:
**FY2025 Q2 dividend per share:** Equinix paid a quarterly common-stock cash dividend of **$4.69 per share**, paid on **June 18, 2025** to shareholders of record on **May 21, 2025**. [[1]]

**REIT payout policy:** In its Q2 2025 Form 10-Q, Equinix stated that it expected its **2025 quarterly and other applicable distributions to equal or exceed REIT taxable income recognized in 2025**. [[2]] Equinix elected REIT tax status beginning in 2015; dividends paid are generally deductible against taxable income of the REIT and qualified REIT subsidiaries, while taxable REIT subsidiaries remain subject to corporate income tax. [[1]] 

Thus, the relevant policy is not a fixed percentage of GAAP earnings or AFFO; it is to distribute at least its REIT taxable income—consistent with maintaining REIT qualification—with the company indicating an intention to distribute the entire taxable income generated by its REIT and qualified REIT subsidiaries for 2025. [[1]]

Related coverage:
**Equinix (EQIX) dividend:** the current quarterly common-stock dividend is **$5.16 per share**, a 10% increase, payable March 18, 2026 to shareholders of record February 25, 2026. [[1]] 
Annualizing that rate implies **$20.64 per share**, subject to future board declarations. [[1]] 

For comparison, Equinix distributed **$4.69 per share per quarter**, or **$18.76 annualized**, during 2025. [[2]]

**REIT payout:** a REIT must distribute at least **90% of REIT taxable income**—calculated before the dividends-paid deduction and excluding net capital gains—to preserve REIT qualification; this is a tax-income test, not an AFFO payout-ratio target. [[3]] [[4]] 

Using Equinix’s 2026 guidance, expected cash dividends of approximately **$2.036 billion** represent about **48.0%–49.0% of guided AFFO** of $4.158–$4.238 billion; on a per-share basis, the $20.64 annualized dividend is about **48.3%–49.2%** of guided diluted AFFO per share of $41.93–$42.74. [[5]] 

Thus, Equinix’s cash dividend is roughly a **48%–49% AFFO payout**, while its legally required REIT distribution percentage is measured against taxable income and is at least 90%. [[5]] [[3]]

private_messages.content:
**Equinix — Dividend & REIT Payout Policy (FY 2025 – 2026)**  

| Metric | Period | Figure | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Quarterly common‑stock dividend** | Q2 2025 | $4.69 per share (paid June 18 2025) | S8.1 |
| **Quarterly common‑stock dividend** | Q1 2026 (most recent increase) | $5.16 per share (10% increase from Q2 2025; payable March 18 2026) | S8.3 |

| **2025 annualized dividend** | 2025 | $18.76 per share (based on $4.69 × 4) | S8.2 |

| **Per‑share AFFO payout** | FY 2026 | $20.64 ÷ $41.93–$42.74 = 48.3%–49.2% of guided diluted AFFO per share | S8.5 |
| **REIT qualification requirement** | Ongoing | Must distribute ≥ 90% of REIT taxable income (calculated before the dividends‑paid deduction, excluding net capital gains) | S8.2, S8.4 |
| **Equinix’s stated distribution intention** | 2025 | Expected 2025 quarterly and other applicable distributions to equal or exceed 2025 REIT taxable income | S8.2 |

**Key take‑aways**

- Equinix has increased its quarterly dividend for 11 consecutive years since its REIT conversion, raising it from $4.69 (Q2 2025) to $5.16 (Q1 2026), a 10% step‑up.  
- The company’s **cash dividend is roughly 48%–49% of guided AFFO**, a level that comfortably exceeds the **minimum 90% of REIT taxable income** required for REIT qualification.  
- The REIT payout policy is **not a fixed AFFO ratio** but a **tax‑income test**: Equinix targets distributions that equal or exceed its REIT taxable income each year, thereby maintaining its REIT status.  
- For 2026, the projected $2.036 B in cash dividends represents about **48%–49%** of the $4.158–4.238 B guided AFFO, and about **48.3%–49.2%** on a per‑share basis.
